clue.text: Making a hole in state funds

indicators.note: the word in tells us the hole is placed inside the abbreviated state

parts.note: Cal. is an abbreviation for the US state of California
a pit is a hole dug in the ground

explanation.surface: Someone is draining a government's public money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a hole in state' reads as raiding the treasury, but it is A and PIT put inside CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital is money available for investment, a synonym for funds.

clue.text: Fed-up over closure, and putting up some resistance

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the preceding word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written before turning
a closure is an ending or conclusion

explanation.surface: Someone sick of a shutdown is resisting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed-up' looks like 'annoyed' but splits into FED and the reversal signal 'up', giving DEF; 'over' places it above ENDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Defending means guarding against attack, so offering resistance.

clue.text: The department is within his grasp, he readily admits

indicators.note: admits means the following words let the solution in, so it is carried inside them

explanation.surface: A manager readily concedes that the whole department is under his control.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere is a field of activity or domain, like a department.

clue.text: Make a song about men rowing, so driving a point home

indicators.note: about means the song word goes round the rowers

parts.note: to make a song is to sing
a crew is a team of oarsmen

explanation.surface: Someone sings about oarsmen to drive home their point.
explanation.walkthrough: SING is placed around CREW, giving S-CREW-ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwing is turning a threaded fastener so its tip drives into the material.

clue.text: Dissentient male suffering breakdown got quite emotional

indicators.note: something suffering a breakdown falls apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dissenting man has a breakdown and becomes very emotional.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sentimentalised is to be made mawkishly feeling, close to overcome by sentiment.

clue.text: Genuine high spots for American estate agents

parts.note: genuine means real
tors are rocky hilltops, especially on Dartmoor in England

explanation.surface: Authentic hilltop properties advertised by US property sellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Realtor is the US word for someone who sells houses and land.

clue.text: Offal can be used to make a stew

indicators.note: the letters can be put to use in a new order to form another word

explanation.surface: A cook notes that offcuts of meat can go into a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offal' suggests meat for the stew, but here it carries its older sense of refuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal originally meant refuse or rubbish, the sense of waste.

clue.text: Detail controlled rising charge

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, from the end back

parts.note: to run a business is to control it, so controlled is ran
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: A tax office explains a rate rise that it set.
explanation.definitionFit: To detail is to give a full account, as to recount or tell a story.

clue.text: Appearance enhanced? That's just not true

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is wearing cosmetics; the other is a fiction invented by someone.

clue.text: Beastly accommodation, but it ensured survival

definitions.text: Beastly accommodation, but it ensured survival

parts.words: Beastly accommodation, but it ensured survival
parts.note: lodging for beasts in the Bible's Flood story, the vessel that preserved every species two by two

explanation.definitionFit: The biblical vessel housed the animals, saving them from the Flood.

clue.text: A hold-up at sea

parts.note: not a robbery by pirates but something that keeps a person afloat in the water

explanation.definitionFit: A buoyant ring thrown to someone overboard holds them up in the water.

clue.text: The outlaw of ancient Egypt

parts.note: taken as written
to outlaw something is to ban it

explanation.surface: A criminal from the time of the pharaohs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outlaw' reads as a noun but works as the verb meaning prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a great city of ancient Egypt, and this adjective describes things from it.

clue.text: May dread changes. Fancy!

indicators.note: the letters change their order to give a new word

explanation.surface: May fears change. Imagine that!
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a whimsical imagining, the same as a reverie.

clue.text: Aristocrats without honour —- they depend on listening devices

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the nobles go round the honour

parts.note: earls are British noblemen
the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

explanation.surface: Untitled nobles rely on bugging equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depend' is used literally: these fleshy lobes hang down from ears, the listening devices.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft lower lobes hang below each ear, which is the organ of hearing.

clue.text: Engaging relation in outdoor exercise

indicators.note: engaging here means holding or taking in, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: open, as in open air, means outdoor
a ratio is a numerical relation between quantities

explanation.surface: A charming relative takes part in an open-air workout.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is a military exercise or manoeuvre.

clue.text: Atheists may be converted, with the utmost celerity

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unbelievers may be won over to the faith very quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of hasty, meaning quickest or most rushed.

clue.text: Only the male worker will accept direction still

indicators.note: will accept means the joined pair takes another letter into itself

parts.note: a stag party is for men only
a worker ant is the standard crossword worker
N is north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Only the man doing the job will take instructions without moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water is motionless, not flowing.

clue.text: Copper held up by traffic, resulting in abuse

indicators.note: held means the trade word keeps the metal inside it

parts.note: traffic as in drug traffic means trade

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the symbol is read upwards

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer stuck in traffic responds with insults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal, giving CU, turned to UC and put inside TRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: To traduce someone is to slander or speak ill of them.

clue.text: A town with more to offer?

parts.note: and joins things together, like with
over means extra or left over, more than needed

explanation.surface: A tourist board asks which town has more to offer.
explanation.walkthrough: Andover is a market town in Hampshire, southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Andover is a named town in Hampshire, England.

clue.text: Pop back with mother maybe when exposed

indicators.note: back means the word for dad is read backwards

parts.note: pa and pop both mean father
a mother is one example of a parent

explanation.surface: Dad returns with Mum, perhaps when found out.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means plainly visible, as something exposed is open to view.

clue.text: Sound location for fish

indicators.note: the word Sound signals that a word is said out loud and spelt differently

parts.note: a place is a location

explanation.surface: A good spot for fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'healthy' or a sea channel but signals a soundalike.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a European flatfish caught for food.

clue.text: Authority for parking a vehicle in the street

indicators.note: in means the vehicle phrase is put inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
a van is a road vehicle

explanation.surface: A council official rules on leaving a car parked in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parking' joins the pieces in the surface; the container is 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A savant is a learned person, an authority on a subject.

clue.text: Active, so needs a drink about four

indicators.note: about means the drink goes around the number

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone lively needs a beer at around four o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Alive can mean lively and active, as in alert to things.

clue.text: Nothing doing!

parts.note: read not as a refusal but literally, a state in which nothing is being done

explanation.definitionFit: Idleness, the absence of any activity, is literally nothing being done.

clue.text: The cat about nine exhibits some frailty

indicators.note: about means the cat word goes round the number

parts.note: puss is a familiar name for a cat
taken as written, the word nine

explanation.surface: A cat with nine lives turns out to be rather weak.
explanation.definitionFit: Puniness is smallness and weakness, a degree of frailty.

clue.text: A plant which has many an admirer

parts.note: C is a hundred in Roman numerals, standing for many
a lover is someone who admires

explanation.surface: A flower with a large number of fans.
explanation.definitionFit: Clover is a low-growing plant with three-lobed leaves.

clue.text: Let out about a certain point being objected to

indicators.note: about means the let word goes round the compass point

parts.note: a let property is rented out
SE, south-east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Releasing someone over a particular point caused offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let out' reads as release but means rented.
explanation.definitionFit: Resented means taken badly, felt as an offence and protested.
